Looping in with the technical constraints we'll validate. Short summary of what I'll test against Acme's network: 

- CIDR guidance: Prefer we see a /22 for the enclave (minimum /24 per subnet for availability). Avoid 10.0.0.0/8 overlapping our control plane (we use 10.128.0.0/14 internally).
- BGP: If we peer, we expect a single advertised ASN from Acme; we'll request a specific route filter to only accept the agreed prefixes.
- NAT: Hairpin NAT is required for internal to internal egress that returns via the public egress IP — confirm that the firewall preserves source ports.
- Ports (minimum):
  * TCP 443 (outbound TLS for model downloads and telemetry)
  * TCP 8443 (control-plane webhooks, if used)
  * UDP 123 (optional NTP), note devices behind NAT might need port mapping
  * TCP 22 (jumpbox, restricted, logged)
  * High ephemeral range (10240-65535) for KV/cache connections — we can prefer a smaller ephemeral range if Acme wants to auditable WHITELIST

Firewall example allowlist (to give Acme a concise entry):
- Allow outbound TCP 443 to *.redwood-hosted.net
- Allow outbound TCP 8443 to specific control-plane ip ranges (will supply)
- Allow inbound from Redwood for health-checks (source: 52.34.12.0/24) on TCP 8080

MTU: We recommend 9000 only if all intermediate devices support jumbo frames. Default to 1500 for the initial test to reduce fragmentation risk.

I'll draft a single-page network validation file to hand to Acme's firewall admin (example attached).

- Ben

Perfect — thanks for the quick turn.

I've attached a concise runbook (zt-seg-checklist.xlsx) and included the minimum smoke-test script below so your ops can validate quickly on Dec 12. If everything passes we'll follow the rollout playbook in the runbook and keep a 2-hour monitoring window.

Smoke-test (10 steps, ~30 mins):
1) Validate control-plane reachability (TCP 443) from enclave hosts to our control-plane IPs
2) Confirm model artifact pull over TLS (simulate a 50MB model fetch)
3) Verify KV/cache ephemeral connections (open/close 10x)
4) Run a 1-minute low-latency generation against a pinned model to confirm inference path
5) Simulate KMS key rotation (confirm no downtime for decryption path)
6) Validate logs delivery to your SIEM (sample event)
7) Confirm egress IP mapping (public IP 54.210.11.45 seen by outbound call)
8) Health-check probe from Redwood (expect 200 on /health)
9) Restore/rollback: disable routing to Redwood and verify application fails closed
10) Post-test: collect kernel packet drops and MTU error counters

If Dec 12 09:00 PT works, we'll book the slot and Ben/Kimberly/Priyom will be on the call for troubleshooting.

Thanks — attaching: zt-seg-checklist.xlsx
